loci.rationale: NOTICE constant: the scoped processing information (controller, purposes, consent basis, limits, rights) that must be made available at collection and in the source-specific import notice.
notice() renders NOTICE as a details block; the means by which the information is made available in the UI.
Direct collection: the /apply form fields include notice() before submission, so the notice is presented at collection.
Entrypoint for direct collection: POST /apply routes to store.submit.
submit() stores the application and records the 'application' event referencing the notice version; the collection-side state change.
Entrypoint for the indirect import: POST /case/<id>/verify routes to store.action op 'verify'.
verify action writes the source-specific 'partner notice' event (Income Registry, underwriting purpose, plus NOTICE) into the case inbox — the Art. 14 notice delivery.
Downstream use: case history renders events (including the partner notice) in the case inbox, making the notice retrievable by the applicant.

output.path_summary: Direct collection: POST /apply (app.py 0083-0084) -> store.submit (store.py 0065-0083) records the case and an 'application' event citing the notice version; the NOTICE (store.py 0009) is presented on the application form via views.notice() (views.py 0024-0025, 0031). Indirect import: officer POST /case/<id>/verify (app.py 0097-0098) -> store.action 'verify' (store.py 0157-0160) writes a 'partner notice' event naming the Income Registry and underwriting purpose plus NOTICE into the case inbox; the event is rendered in the case history (views.py 0076, 0079) and NOTICE is also returned as processing_information by store.access (store.py 0120). Both notice paths are present in source; the import notice is recorded to the inbox regardless of whether the applicant opens the case.
missing_boundaries: No execution, browsing or retrieval was performed; assessment is static source reading only.
Whether the applicant opens the case inbox is a scenario variable; the code records the notice to the inbox but delivery timing/feasibility beyond recording is not verifiable from source.
The verify notice is only produced when an officer performs 'verify'; the code does not itself trigger the import or the notice automatically.
Adequacy of NOTICE wording against Art. 13(1)-(2)/14(1)-(3) content elements is judged only from the constant text, not from legal interpretation of completeness.
No claim is made about upstream or hidden implementation.
